description: OverridesStore cross-SDK conformance: pluggable persistence for system.control.update_config and system.control.toggle_feature. The interface is the whole-map form all three SDKs ship (decision D-47): `load() -> mapping` and `save(mapping)`. An earlier revision of this fixture and of features/system-modules.md described a per-key surface — set(key,value) / get(key) / get_all() / delete(key) — that NO SDK implements; three independent implementations agreeing against a spec sentence is the spec being wrong, not three bugs.

test_cases.description: After save() returns, the override is durable: a fresh FileOverridesStore reading the same path MUST observe the value in the mapping returned by load().
On APCore startup with both a base apcore.yaml and an overrides file, override values MUST take precedence over base values for the same key. The base file is unmodified.
InMemoryOverridesStore behaves identically to FileOverridesStore for load() and save() but performs no disk I/O. Two separate InMemoryOverridesStore instances do NOT share state.
Constructing FileOverridesStore with a path that does not yet exist MUST succeed (treat as empty store). load() MUST return an empty mapping; the first save() MUST create the file.
Removing a key is a read-modify-write: load(), drop the key, save() the remaining map. A subsequent load() MUST NOT include it. Saving a map that never contained the key is a no-op.

driver_contract.interface: Drive `load()` and `save(mapping)` only. A single-key change is a read-modify-write: load the map, set or remove the key, save the whole map back. That is what the sys-modules code paths actually do.
driver_contract.durability: For FileOverridesStore, 'persisted' means observable through a FRESHLY CONSTRUCTED store on the same path — not through the instance that wrote it, which could satisfy the assertion from memory.
driver_contract.isolation: Two InMemoryOverridesStore instances MUST NOT share state.
